incident_a_pool_exhaustion.root_cause: Deploy v2.4.1 reduced payment-gateway-adapter connection pool from 50 to 10 at 14:30. Under normal traffic the pool saturates, causing intermittent ConnectionPoolTimeoutException / GATEWAY_TIMEOUT charge failures. Multiple independent sources corroborate this (KI-101, RB-014, INC-2031, logs, deploy history).

supporting_evidence.excerpt: 2026-09-02 14:47:12 ERROR payment-gateway-adapter ConnectionPoolTimeoutException: no available connection after 5000ms
v2.4.1 2026-09-02 14:30 payment-gateway-adapter Reduced connection pool size from 50 to 10 (memory optimization for the upcoming cost-reduction initiative)

KI-101: A ConnectionPoolTimeoutException in payment-gateway-adapter logs is a known signature of an undersized connection pool relative to current traffic; cross-reference against deployment history for any recent pool size change

RB-014: Payment Gateway Timeout Spike Symptoms: ConnectionPoolTimeoutException appearing in payment-gateway-adapter logs; intermittent (not total) payment failures; payment-service logging GATEWAY_TIMEOUT. Diagnostic steps: 1....
INC-2031 (2026-03-14) Summary: Intermittent payment failures, payment-gateway-adapter logging ConnectionPoolTimeoutException under normal (not elevated) traffic....
payment-gateway-adapter: owns a bounded connection pool to the external Payment Provider's API.
Timeout: the adapter waits up to 5000ms to acquire a pooled connection

incident_a_pool_exhaustion.remediation: 1) Revert payment-gateway-adapter pool size to baseline 50 (undo v2.4.1). 2) Redeploy payment-gateway-adapter. 3) Confirm the ERROR signature stops and requests succeed. Typical recovery ~20 minutes (RB-014).

incident_b_ambiguous_delay.root_cause: Order confirmation emails sit in the notification-service queue for 40-75 minutes before send; one elevated queue-depth warning exists, with no ERROR-level failures. The bottleneck (undersized consumers vs third-party email provider latency) cannot be confirmed - consumer/provider metrics are uninstrumented, and there is no matching known issue, correlated deploy, or prior incident.

supporting_evidence.excerpt: 2026-08-15 11:10:02 WARN notification-service Queue depth elevated: 340 messages. Delays are consistently 40-75 minutes between Email queued and Email sent.
Deployment history No deployment touched notification-service in the month before this incident (2026-08-15).
KI-114: Notification email formatting glitch - Cosmetic only; template fix scheduled
RB-002: Elevated Notification Queue Depth Symptoms: notification-service logging elevated queue depth warnings. Diagnostic steps: check consumer count and downstream email provider latency....
Previous incidents No previous incident in the historical record involves notification-service email delivery latency.
notification-service: subscribes to an internal message queue; each order/payment event is queued as a message, and a pool of consumer workers dequeues and sends the corresponding email.

incident_b_ambiguous_delay.remediation: 1) Do not treat this as a confirmed root cause - flag for human review. 2) Inspect notification-service queue depth and consumer count now. 3) Check third-party email provider status/latency. 4) Add per-stage timing (queue wait vs provider send) before any permanent scale change. Scaling consumers is unverified (RB-002).
